# DG0 round 18, code-security review: **FAIL**

The gate should not pass on this candidate. One of the sandbox's core claims is wrong: runs are not kept apart from each other. One agent can write into another agent's work while both are running at the same time.

I checked that I was reviewing the right code. HEAD (`ccb989f`) only adds metadata after the freeze. The candidate ID I recomputed, `sha256:21efe44b…023cc5`, matches for commit `450c756`. I didn't read any other reviewer's round-18 record.

## Checks
- **Test suite:** `node --test` on the gate and agent tests passed 91 of 91, with none skipped.
- **Pre-freeze:** `prefreeze.sh DG0` passed all 11 checks in a fresh clone (exit 0).
- **Changes since round 17:** only the D-032 fix in `agent_sandbox.py` and one new test.
- **CI workflow:** unchanged and correctly locked down (read-only permissions, actions pinned by SHA, full git history, a failed check fails the job).
- **Secrets:** the scan of tracked files found no credentials.

## New findings
- **F-DG0-152 (High, mandatory violation, owner `delivery-orchestrator`).** The sandbox binds the host's `/proc` read-write and shares the host's process namespace, and every run has the same uid and capabilities (`agent_sandbox.py:147-180`). So a process at the file-tool layer can reach another concurrent run's files through `/proc/<peer-pid>/root` or `/proc/<peer-pid>/cwd`.
  - I rebuilt two runs side by side from the real `agent_sandbox.py` arguments, in a throwaway fixture. The attacker's direct write to QA's evidence was refused.
  - The same writes through `/proc` succeeded. They reached the victim's evidence, its private scratch clones, its staged review record and its session (transcript) directory. They also worked through a symlink, which is how a file tool could get past the write guard's check-then-write race.
  - The victim's own copy-back then accepted the forged record as its own (exit 0, nothing discarded), so the runner would commit it.
  - This breaks a control the threat model lists as mechanically prevented, and it makes residuals 7 and 8 larger than disclosed.
  - **Limits of the proof:** I deliberately did not probe the live peer runs, so this isn't shown end to end against a real run. I also didn't test whether the validator's transcript-replay check would catch a forged record.
  - **Proposed fix:** put each run in its own Landlock domain that only restricts cross-run access. The kernel supports this (Landlock ABI 7). In my test it blocked the cross-run writes and signals, own areas stayed writable, and nested bwrap with a fresh `--proc` (what the pre-freeze needs) still worked. Other options are a separate uid per run, or running reviewers one at a time.
- **F-DG0-153 (Low, not mandatory).** `threat-model.md:27` still says the sandbox "creates no PID/IPC namespace of its own", but the code unshares IPC. The code and `sandbox.json` are correct; I'd accept this as an observation.

## Earlier findings
| Finding | Result | Status after |
|---|---|---|
| F-DG0-150 | PASS: the old code crashes (exit 1, no `sandbox.json`); the new code records a write-once discard (exit 3), keeps processing later files and doesn't follow a planted symlink | CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG0-151 | PASS: the module docstring now matches the code | CLOSED_VERIFIED |
| F-DG0-147 | Still reproduces, still Low and fails closed | ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION |
| F-DG0-149 | FAIL: assessed without writing to `/proc/sys`; the residual is larger than disclosed because of F-DG0-152 | OPEN |

The round-17 concurrency fix (D-031) and the private IPC namespace (F-DG0-148) both still hold.

## Other
- My requirements checked: REQ-DLV-007, 013, 016, 022, 023 and 026. Of these, REQ-DLV-007 has the failing check.
- Part of one earlier response was stopped by the safety classifier. The check it contained had already run and its output is logged. I didn't redo or extend that work.
- The disposable clones have been removed. The leftover test directories are in this run's private `$TMPDIR`, which the runner deletes.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-18/`:
- code-security-reviewer.json (the review record; it validates against the schema and every evidence path exists)
- code-security-reviewer.findings.json
- code-security-reviewer.verifications.json

Reproduction scripts and logs are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-18/`.
